question: Each server answers slowly one time in 100. A search waits for replies from 100 servers at once. How often is it slow?
answer: About 63 in 100 searches. A search is fast only if all 100 servers are, and the chance of that is 0.99 to the power 100, about 37%. Google's Jeffrey Dean and Luiz Barroso used this to explain why big services resend slow requests. A rare delay per machine becomes the usual delay per user.
move: When everything must go right at once, small risks multiply fast.
trap: Each server is fine 99% of the time, so the whole seems fine.
source: Dean & Barroso, Communications of the ACM, 2013
reference: Dean & Barroso, The Tail at Scale, Communications of the ACM 56(2), 2013
